utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Tieger, is the Prosecution ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, may I then again remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Tieger: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can we move ahead to a letter dated January 15th, 1992. It can be found at tab 80. It is presently shown on the screen. Can you tell us what this letter represents, what it depicts.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a letter signed by Rajko Dukic, as president of the Executive Committee of the SDS sent to the -- what he describes as the Serbian ministries in the government of BH. As the Court can see, it informs him of a decision of the Executive Committee held at the end of 1991, on 30 December, that the Serbian ministries in BH have set up contacts regarding joint plans and work programmes with the corresponding ministers, ministries, and other government bodies and institutions in the government of the Republic of Serbia. This is obviously a reflection of the desire of the Bosnian Serb leadership to maintain close cooperation with the Republic of Serbia. And I would point out one interesting facet of this letter, is that it is a letter from a party organ to the Serbian ministries, which are of course state organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move next to a document found at tab 82 of the binder. That is the 2nd Session of the Council of Ministers held on January 17th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the only other session of the Council of Ministers that we have a record of, that is, a record of one of its sessions. Again, if we can magnify the second paragraph, we can see some of the people present, and the second highlighted paragraph, which is I think the fourth paragraph on the page, you can see the additional people that were present, that is, those who were not members of the Ministerial Council, including Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, Dr. Koljevic, Mr. Dukic, and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also highlighted a portion on page 4 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you allow me to just go back once to what we find on tab 80 and ask for a clarification? I'm sorry to interrupt you. The letter of Mr. Dukic, Mr. Treanor. I read from the transcript that this letter informs him of a decision of the Executive Committee held at the end of 1991, of 30 December, that the Serbian ministries in BH have set up contacts regarding joint plans and work programmes with the corresponding ministers, ministries, and other government bodies in the government of the Republic of Serbia. Could you indicate to me where I find that it's Serbian ministries that have set up. I do see that the latter comes from the Executive Committee.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is addressed to the Serbian ministries in the government of BH. I take that to mean the -- basically the members of the Bosnian Serb Ministerial Council that was established on the 21st of December, which is composed of the SDS-designated members of the government of BH who were actually ministers, or if there was no -- they did not have a ministry in the given ministry, the deputy minister, but I think it's addressed to that group of individuals, the Bosnian Serb Ministerial Council, which was composed, in fact, of high functionaries of the BH government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not see that explicitly in the letter, but you would agree that your interpretation of -- on behalf of whom the Executive Committee addresses the Serbian ministries, that it's not a direct contact between the Executive Committee, but, as you say, the Ministerial Council that just had been established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is a letter from the chairman of the Executive Committee, again, to the Serbian ministries, informing them of a decision of the Executive Committee and asking them to implement it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I read your testimony that the Serbian ministries in BH have set up contacts regarding joint plans and work programmes with the corresponding ministers, ministries, and other government bodies in the government of the Republic of Serbia. I'm wondering where I can read in this letter that the contacts have been set up between the Serbian ministries in BH, on the one hand side --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. If I said that, I misspoke. They have to set up contacts. They should set up contacts regarding joint plans and work programmes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then my understanding of your testimony should be that this letter addresses the Serbian ministries, more or less inviting them to get in close contact with their Serbian BH counterparts; is that a...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's requesting them to implement the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not clear from the letter, at least, with whom. Because I see only -- I see that the letter is sent by the Executive Committee. It is addressed to the Serbian ministries in the BH government. I see that from the -- since it is addressed to the BH government, it is an instruction for them to seek contact with the Serbian ministries; is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Where it says "you" in the letter, "You are kindly requested," that refers to the Serbian ministries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's what they have to do and not what they had done yet, as your testimony says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you had just turned your attention to page 4 of the English transcript of the 2nd Session of the Council of Ministers and to the highlighted portion in that document that is now shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this paragraph relaying to the work programme of the Council of Ministers, we see the issue of regionalisation being addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, that is the paragraph that is enumerated number 4 and headed, "The draft work programme of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of the Serbian People of BH." That highlight continues to the bottom of that page, the last sentence of which indicates: "Way as to enlarge the territory of the regions and encompass a larger number of," and then it continues on to the next page, reading: "Inhabitants, wherever possible, in order to consolidate the regions, both ethnicically and economically."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Treanor, you've also highlighted a portion of that document found on page 5 of the English translation, and that is the paragraph enumerated number 8: "Realisation of the conclusions reached at the 1st meeting of the Ministerial Council of the Assembly of Serbian People of BH."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This again relates to the issue of regionalisation. A reference is made to Mr. Cizmovic, who, on the 21st of December, was designated by the Bosnian Serb Assembly as the coordinator of the work of the governments of the SAOs, the Serbian autonomous districts, and was also at that time made a member of the Ministerial Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's one final highlight on page 5. I'm sorry. That would be page 6, Your Honour. That's the paragraph enumerated number 4 on that page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an interesting remark by Mr. Krajisnik, interesting observation on the division of labour between the Assembly, the Ministerial Council, and the SDS, that this may be a reference to the letter we just considered from -- the letter from Mr. Dukic to the Serbian ministries, which, as I pointed out, was a letter from a party organ to state organs. This may have been the type of thing that Mr. Krajisnik was referring to and was concerned about, apparently feeling that the lines of authority were being crossed here, confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document selected by Mr. Treanor is found at tab 83. This is a document entitled, "Regionalisation, demographic, economic, and other significant aspects," and is dated January 1992, from Sarajevo. I note that you've highlighted one page of that document, which is found at page 9 and is presently shown on the screen. Perhaps you can tell us quickly about the document and the particular page that is shown.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is apparently the material that the Ministerial Council asked Dr. Skoko to prepare. Yesterday I misidentified Dr. Skoko as an official in the BH Statistical Institute. He was actually in the Institute for Social Planning. At any rate, he was asked to prepare material in connection with regionalisation, under a title very similar, if not exact, to this report, which is regionalisation, demographic, economic, and other essential aspects. And I'd just like to call the Court's attention in particular to this graph, which illustrates one of the points made in the report and reflects a concern that we have seen continually expressed by Bosnian Serb leaders, namely, the demographic factor as far as the position of the Serbs in BH is concerned, their fear that soon the Muslims in BH would become a majority throughout the republic and be in a position to institute in some occasions a -- expressed the fear of an Islamic state being established, that sort of thing, but in any case, reducing the Serbs to a -- definitely reducing the Serbs to a minority within BH, and this graph presents projections of population growth in two different variants. As you can see, both of those variants result in a fairly rapid increase of the Muslim population as opposed to the stable and even declining Serbian and Croatian population. Now, what these variants are and what they're based on statistically, I don't know, not being a demographer, but this is a very, if I can use the term, graphic illustration of the Serbian demographic concerns, which was one of the underlying factors in their drive for regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can turn next to an intercepted telephone conversation between -- or involving Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic, which is found in the intercept binder at tab 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps before we move forwards, could -- Mr. Treanor, could you tell us something about the source of this document, to whom it was presented? Perhaps I missed it, but at least it doesn't become clear from the document itself, as far as I can see. It's a rather lengthy document, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The document itself does not indicate who it was delivered to or who precisely the author was. As I mentioned, however, the title is very similar to the materials that the Council of Ministers requested Mr. Skoko to prepare at their first session. And it is, in fact, dated January 1992, and it was recovered from the papers of the SDS and its members that were gathered by the Bosnian authorities after the Bosnian Serb leaders and the SDS officials left Sarajevo in April and May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So do I understand that you consider it possible and even perhaps you think it's likely that this document was presented to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no. The Council of Ministers, again, requested such a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if we can go back to the minutes of the 1st Ministerial Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We have that on the screen now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's item number 2 on page 3 of the original: "Material entitled regionalisation: Demographic, economic and other indicators should be updated and completed by 17 January. And the material regionalisation and monetary flows should be finished by 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. January." Dr. Milorad Skoko is responsible for these tasks. And I say, the similar -- the title of the document we were just considering is very similar to this. There is another document in the collection dated September 1991 that is similar to this January report, so it, obviously, represents an update of that report. Given the similarity of the title, the process of the -- compiling of the report and the dates concerned, I can draw the conclusion -- I do draw the conclusion, but it is only a conclusion, based on those factors, that this is the report that Dr. Skoko was asked to prepare. Now, as I say, we only have minutes of two sessions of the Ministerial Council, and we do not, in fact, see this being presented on the 17th of January. So whether it was ever presented to the Ministerial Council or not, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Thank you for your clarification. I think we now move to the intercept, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what is under discussion here is the idea of a referendum in BH. It is not clear from the -- precisely clear to me from the context of the conversation what the exact date of this conversation is. The transcript only indicates January 1992. But by way of background to this referendum issue, which is one that will dominate public discussion in Bosnia for the next month or so, certainly through the end of February/beginning of March 1992, when the referendum was in fact held, I would just remind the Court that the non-Serbian members of the BH Presidency and government had responded to the invitation of the European Community at the end of 1991 to seek recognition. The European Community had established a commission to examine the requests of the republics of Yugoslavia that sought international recognition as independent states, to see whether they fulfilled certain conditions. On the 11th of January, the so-called Badinter Commission issued a report in relation to Bosnia and Herzegovina. This report indicates that it took into consideration a number of documents and factors, including, of course, the requests of the non-Serbian members of the Bosnian state organs, but also the -- some documents and activities of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. In view of the obvious contradiction between the stand being taken by the non-Serbian members of the BH government organs and the Bosnian Serb organs, in this case, the Assembly, the commission in its report -- and I would just quote from the very end of the report, where the commission indicates its opinion that: "The will of the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina to constitute the SRBH as a sovereign and independent state cannot be held to have been fully established. This assessment could be reviewed if appropriate guarantees were provided by the republic applying for recognition, possibly by means of a referendum of all the citizens of the SRBH, without distinction, carried out under international supervision." So the subject of such a referendum became the subject of public debate in BH in the days following that, and I think as we will see shortly, there was a session, a joint session of the BH Assembly, held on the 25th -- I believe it was the 25th of January, going late into the -- or early into the next morning, which in fact adopted a decision that such a referendum be held. This decision was adopted in a fashion similar to the way in which the decision adopting the memorandum and platform in October 1991 was adopted, that is, Mr. Krajisnik, as the presiding officer, closed the session, but the session was reconvened later by the deputy president of the Assembly in the absence of the SDS deputies, and the decision was taken. This caused some outrage among the Bosnian Serb deputies and other members of the Bosnian Serb leadership, and there was some -- a fair amount of discussion, as I think we may be seeing, as to what line the Bosnian Serbs should take in regard to this referendum. And here Mr. Krajisnik is recommending to Dr. Karadzic what their public position should be on this issue. It closely reflects what, in fact, became the stance of the SDS leadership in regard to the referendum, which was basically as follows: They regarded the decision to have the referendum as illegitimate, but they were perfectly willing to see the members of the other two national communities in BH, that is, the Muslims and the Croats, go ahead and have a vote, similar to the vote that the Serbs had already had. The Serbs had their vote, so let the others have theirs. But it will be their vote, not ours, and cannot bind us. On the other hand, if we can come to an agreement as to -- in regard to the transformation of BH, then we would then have the conditions to, in fact, have a referendum of all the peoples in BH. But until such an agreement had been reached, such a referendum was premature and any vote that was taken could only be considered to be a vote expressing the will of the Muslim and Croat national communities in BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you referred to a session of the Bosnian Assembly held on January 25th, and the conclusions resulting from that. Was a session of the Serbian Assembly held shortly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The session of the Bosnian Assembly went until very early in the morning. The SDS deputies had left earlier. I think it went until 5.00 o'clock in the morning, something like that. But the Bosnian Serb members of the -- what was now the Assembly of the Serbian People in BH called a session of their Assembly later on the 26th, beginning at 11.15 in the morning, and this session was called exclusively to consider the events of the night before the decision to call a referendum, other decisions that were taken in their absence, and to air their views on that and discuss what they should do as a way forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the English transcript of that session is found as the first document in binder 8 and is at tab 84.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the first section of that transcript which you have highlighted is found at page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These excerpts, as with the other Assembly sessions, will, I hope, give the Court an idea course of the discussions in the session and bring out some of the more salient points. Here we have Mr. Goran Zekic speaking. Mr. Zekic was a -- had been elected as a deputy to the Chamber of Citizens of the BH Assembly and was also a member of the SDS Main Board. And he addresses in his remarks themes such as BH is now being a prison for the Serbs and emphasising that it should be possible to divide the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the first -- there's three highlighted sections on page 3, the first of which is the sentence: "What should be drummed into the world and Europe is that they must not defence us in some sort of Bosnia-Herzegovina pin in which the Serbian people should stay put like in some detention camp." The second highlighted sentence begins -- the second highlighted portion begins approximately two sentences after that, with the words: "For this reason alone, we should be aware that Bosnia and Herzegovina is no more." Discusses Alija's assertion that someone should show how Bosnia and Herzegovina can be partitioned. And continues that: "His ignorance is no obstacle. Bosnia and Herzegovina can be and must be partitioned and his ignorance must not stand in our way," is the last sentence of that highlighted portion. And finally the last highlighted portion are the two sentences which begin: "Today we should propose measures and adopt decisions so that, at last, we can actually begin to put into practice our political inclinations," and ends with the sentence which discusses the desire -- "The intention to stay ahead of those who wish to lock us up in some sort of camp which they would then call Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular passage reflects the desire expressed by many of the deputies at this session to now go ahead with all due speed in the preparation of a constitution for the new Serbian Republic and related legislation, establishing its various ministries and other institutions. And the Court will notice the reference to the plebiscite, which is constantly referred to by Bosnian Serb leaders as the source of their policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted section can be found at page 7. The first highlighted section begins after the first sentence of the second paragraph and begins: "By now it is probably clear," and ends with the language: "Better chances for them to claim these lands for themselves and better chances to lord over us."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're on Dr. Karadzic now I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second highlighted portion begins at the last full paragraph of that page: "We must come to our senses," and ends with the language: "So that we can accelerate our preparations for the events that will follow."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, an expression of the desire to continue with the establishment of the organs of a separate Bosnian Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 10 of the English translation, we see the next highlight beginning at the very bottom of the page, the last sentence on that page, and continuing on to page 11.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now here we have Mr. Vjestica speaking, who was elected as a -- in 1990, elected as a deputy to the Chamber of Citizens. And he again addresses the need to adopt the necessary legal documents so that the institutions can be set up of a Bosnian Serb Republic, and also the same thing done on the regional level.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the sentence that began on the previous page, that is, page 10, continues and it's highlighted in the second sentence -- the next sentence after that is also highlighted, ending with the words: "If I can call it that, like the centre." And the next highlighted portion are three sentences beginning with: "The operative plan should also be drawn up to define tasks precisely," and ends with the sentence: "Those who feel unable, should say so now and allow us to select those who can."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would also draw attention to the mention of 15 February as sort of a deadline to complete this work. That is mentioned by others later on in the session as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move to a highlight found at page 13 of the English translation. And as we can see from the page, the speaker is Mr. Cizmovic. The portion you've highlighted is the last full paragraph, which begins: "To solve this problem, I propose that we begin with an urgent operationalisation."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Cizmovic is expressing his opinion that to forge ahead with the establishment of the republic, and he refers not only to the -- a declaration of 9 January on the promulgation of the republic, but also the instructions of the SDS of 19 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that reference is contained in the last sentence of that excerpt, or that highlighted portion, which reads: "Tasks set out in the instructions of 19 December 1991 should be carried out." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted section is found on page 14. It's a continuation of Mr. Vjestica, after a brief comment by Mr. Krajisnik. And the highlighted portion is the last sentence of Mr. Vjestica's comments on that page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, addressing the same theme, that the need for completing the work necessary to, as he puts it, "Complete the job of taking power in our Serbian state."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 18 of the English translation. You've highlighted comments by Mr. Krajisnik on that page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here Mr. Krajisnik is discussing the proposition which I mentioned before, that the transformation of BH would have to be completed and agreed on by the three national communities before the Bosnian Serb leadership would agree to participate in any referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the specifically highlighted portions are the first sentence of the second paragraph shown there, beginning: "In fact, the conclusion is that the Council of Ministers." And the other highlighted portion begins with the word: "It would not be wise for us to oppose this referendum too." And then concludes with the line: "Demand of the Serbian people to remain in a single state is incorporated in it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page of the English translation, page 19, you've also highlighted some additional comments by Mr. Krajisnik. And those are the two sentences: "We will fix the date, as Mr. Vjestica said, we must sit in some sort of permanent session. We must also meet the deadlines."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this is Mr. Krajisnik's agreement with the desire to complete the legislative programme necessary for establishing the state as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to page 20 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This records the adoption of a decision to that effect, that the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. work should be completed, and Mr. Krajisnik here suggests that the deadline of 15 February be agreed on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the portion that begins: "I hereby declare," and ends with the words: "Should not sit and wait for 15 February." If we could turn to the bottom of page 21, which continues on to page 22. You've highlighted another section, also remarks by Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here he's suggesting that the Council of Ministers be asked to draft a document for consideration by the Assembly. The matter under consideration is a rather obscure one, having to do with the annual budgetary balance. But he responds to some criticism from one of the deputies that they had not prepared some of their -- some of the decisions properly, and he responds that: No. In fact, all of the decisions we have adopted have been fully realisable and we have not adopted any unrealistic decisions, nothing that we cannot implement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you for one clarification at this moment, Mr. Treanor. You said that the matter under consideration is a rather obscure one, having to do with the annual budgetary balance. Is that your interpretation of the last words of page 21 and the first words on page 22, where it says: "For the partition balance sheet"? Is that what you refer to, and do you consider the partition balance sheet something to have to do with budget?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is related to financial matters, which are beyond my understanding, Your Honour. What seems to have been proposed is that the assets of the republic be divided among the national communities, or certainly that the incipient Bosnian Serb Republic get its share of the assets of the republic. And one of the deputies is saying: Well, we can't do that, because the annual balance sheet, which I presume is related to the budget, because they do an annual audit on the budget which is adopted by the Assembly, that these types of financial documents will not be ready until March or something like that, under the normal procedures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your explanation. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And for the record, the highlighted portion on that page to which Mr. Treanor and the Court have been referring are the continuation of the previous sentence on the top of that page, which is simply three words, "Partition balance sheet," and then the last two sentences of that paragraph which begin: "And if you want to have a look," and then concludes with the sentence: "And conclusions are instructions to someone to do something."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Treanor, can we turn to page 23 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am following this material, so it is hard for me to follow the English text. Could the Prosecutor please tell me where these excerpts are in the Serbian -- in the versions in Serbian, because I would like to take an active role in following these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the Prosecutor is able to do so, whether Mr. Treanor is better qualified to do it, is, I take it, not of major concern to you, Mr. Krajisnik. I can understand that it's difficult to follow if no references are made to the B/C/S version. So could you please, to the extent possible, Mr. Treanor, refer to the B/C/S portions as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we're going to Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was actually referring to the highlighted portion at the top of the English translation, which I believe --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is Mr. Bjelosevic, or Mr. Krajisnik again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A continuation of --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Mr. Krajisnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you identify for the record the B/C/S page on which that appears.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I hope the ERN number is sufficient. In this particular document, the pagination is not continuous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, do you have ERN numbers on the top of the pages?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. It will be enough for me if he can only give me the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very good. The ERN number of this page is SA025275. And we're looking in the middle of the page of the original, where Mr. Krajisnik speaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the highlighted portion in English begins with the words: "I think that we must issue conclusions in connection with Mr. Vjestica," and ends with the language: "If by then we adopt a constitution or have the basis."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Krajisnik expressing his agreement that the necessary legislation should be drawn up.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Obviously Mr. Krajisnik has not found that particular portion. I think we might have to take the reference to the B/C/S version a little slower so that it allows Mr. Krajisnik the opportunity to locate the particular portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that Mr. Krajisnik is still going through the document. Did you find the page reference, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's all 020579. There's no 03. If this is the file, file 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is tab 84, at least in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Inside in the Serbian version it's also 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Treanor, you were referring to what page exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ERN is SA 025275.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've got the B/C/S version in front of me, Mr. Krajisnik. I found that page. Can you find it as well? Otherwise I should ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have found it. I was told it was 03, not 02.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this misunderstanding having been clarified, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you were about to address that highlighted portion we just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Krajisnik expressing agreement that the Assembly should complete the necessary legislative work as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can move next, then, to an intercept dated February 4th, 1992, found at tab 25 of the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Is this ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This is --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: ERN number of the original transcript, 02079372?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 02079370 is the first page of that transcript, and it's a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Dr. Karadzic. I'm sorry. No. Excuse me. I'm rechecking the ERN you provided was the correct one.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. The transcript I have does not bear an exact date. It just says February 1992. That's why I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for your information, Mr. Krajisnik, we find the B/C/S version always next to the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I might indicate that Mr. Krajisnik has the documents but doesn't actually have the intercepts, because he's able to look at it from the screen. And to listen, of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we have another conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik, discussing various issues and meetings. Many of the references are obscure. However, the reference to a meeting in Doboj, we've been able to clarify to a certain extent. There was a meeting of leaders of three of the Serbian autonomous districts in Doboj on the 5th of February, which would date this intercept, obviously, before that. And we -- the only thing we know about what transpired at that meeting is from a newspaper article, which I think we will be seeing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 85, very quickly. This is another entry from the Grkovic [phoen] diary, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here is the entry for the 5th of February, and it refers to a meeting of the regions of Central Bosnia and Krajina in Doboj, at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 13 February 1992, article from Derventski List is found at tab 86 is depicted on the screen. The first page of that document you've highlighted the first three paragraphs and then the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the newspaper article I referred to that sheds some light on what happened in Doboj. I'll have to refer to the calendar here. The 13th of February was a Thursday, which is the date of the newspaper, and the article refers to -- discusses two meetings which can lead to some confusion in reading the article. It refers to a meeting the previous weekend of the Doboj SDS, and that would have been the weekend of the 8th and the 9th of February. And at that meeting, Mr. Bjelosevic, who I think we just ran into in the Assembly session, gives a report to the people present at that session about the meeting in Doboj. So the first part of this article relates his report about the meeting in Doboj on the 5th of February, which was a Wednesday. And if we could magnify the second two paragraphs, perhaps. The first paragraph, as you can see, indicates some of the people that were present at Doboj, including Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, and Mr. Maksimovic. And the third paragraph indicates that the two main topics of discussion at the Doboj meeting were the referendum, which I said is the issue that dominates political discourse in Bosnia during this period, and the future of Northern Bosnia within the future BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the second page of that document. You've highlighted the first three paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The report indicated on the previous page in one of the highlighted portions that the issue of Northern Bosnia was in fact the issue that attracted greatest interest at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask one question in respect of this article. Bridge to the Krajinas. Comparing the original with the translation, Mr. Treanor, is it correct that the entry or summary which appears just below the title is not translated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that appears to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's not a full translation of what appears in the article? And I'm not now referring to what seems to be above the title, which seems to be a reference to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serbian Democratic Party, it says up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's not translated. And bridge to Krajina is translated. But the next six lines are not translated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, the Chamber is always very happy to either find an indication of parts not being translated or to receive full translations of documents, especially where it says, "full translation" on top of the -- this page. Please proceed. And perhaps you could provide the Chamber with a translation of that part as well, so that we have every information available.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you were referring to the discussion about the meeting as reflected in the paragraphs you've highlighted on page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This highlighted portion reflects the concern about the situation in a portion of Northern Bosnia along the Sava River, which is located between Eastern Bosnia and Western Bosnia, but is not dominated ethnographically by the Serbs, but would be very important as a geographical link between Eastern and Western Bosnia, and indeed beyond Western Bosnia to the Croatian Krajina, the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And the idea here is broached of a transfer of population between -- involving the Croats living in Bosnia along the river and the Serbs living on the other side of the river, in Croatia, in order to consolidate the -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what they refer to as a bridge, ethnographically for the Serbs. Moslavina being an area in Croatia just north of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was about to move on to the next item, but it appeared to me the Court was reviewing the document. I didn't want to move prematurely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just reading it. Mr. Treanor, is the reference to the highway, is that the highway north of the River Sava connecting Belgrade and Zagreb? Is that what reference is made to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says the uncertain route. "Because the highway will be an uncertain route for Serbs for some time to come." I'm just trying to understand what it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that could be a reference to the main highway linking Zagreb and Belgrade, which runs just north of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And north of the frontier between --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- between -- the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, yes, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Croatia, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be the main route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under normal circumstances, but given the war that's going on or the -- well, that had been concluded, but the situation was still very tense there with the establishment of Serbian power in certain parts along that route and the Croatian Republic exercising authority along others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next item, Your Honours, can be found at tab 26 of the intercept binder. It is a conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, who we've met a couple of times, has called Karadzic to inform him about a meeting of Serbian Orthodox bishops which is due to take place in Western Bosnia and suggesting that maybe he or other SDS leaders might like to come. But it moves on from there, as we'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, we started on page 3 of the transcript, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we can see, Dr. Karadzic had to demure on the meeting with the bishops in Western Bosnia and informs Mr. Kupresanin of an upcoming big meeting of SDS leaders, and he indicates who is going to be there, along the lines I've indicated before, basically getting the various groups of SDS party and state office holders together in one meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning very quickly to tab 87, is there an entry in the Grkovic diary reflecting that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the entry for events on the 14th of February, indicating a meeting of the Main and Executive Boards and assemblymen at 1700.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at tab 27 of the intercepts binder you'll find a transcript of a speech by Dr. Karadzic given at that meeting, and that's the next document to which we'll turn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just clarify on that previous document where it's translated as "assemblymen," that is the word that I've been rendering here as "deputies." That is references to the deputies to the Assembly, the Republic Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the first portion of that speech which you have highlighted is found at page 2.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Karadzic gives a rather lengthy address to the assembled officials and covers a variety of topics, including the general political situation and the situation in the party. Here he indicates in this particular sentence a point which I've tried to emphasise before, his recognition of the importance of the -- again, the word here, "representatives" is the same word that I've been rendering as "deputies," as their importance in the -- within the set-up of the SDS and the Bosnian Serb leadership in general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record that is the sentence that begins at line 12 and ends at line 14: "So party officials are not authority to us, authority for us, or first of all the representatives," and so on. Next highlighted portion is found at page 3 of the transcript. And continues on to the next page. It begins at line 27.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in this particular passage, Dr. Karadzic moves on to the theme of establishing control of territory for the republic which has been proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, Mr. Tieger. There seems to be some difference between the text we see on the screen and the text we have in hard copy in front of us. The words, "Especially because we proclaimed," which appear on line 27 on the screen, appear on line 26 on our hard copy. I don't know what could explain the difference, but it seems that the two copies we're working with are not -- at least not exactly the same. I'm not suggesting that there's any major difference or that the content would be different, but I just note that what you refer to as starting at line 27 starts at line 26 in our copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for catching that, Your Honour. First of all, I'll do some checking to see if that slight discrepancy can be explained. And in addition, I will indicate for the record what the highlighted portion is, not simply by reference to the numbers, but by a more precise reference to the selection itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Treanor. Did you want us to continue on to the next page?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd just like to comment about this passage as a bit of background here. I mentioned the opinion of the Badinter Commission, which, among other things, was a tribute to the work of the Bosnian Serb Assembly in that it prevented any outright decision on the recognition of BH. Things have now progressed to the point where the International Conference on the Former Yugoslavia is holding sessions, negotiating sessions, under the auspices of Mr. Cutilheiro, Ambassador Cutilheiro, I believe, of Portugal, and these negotiations included representatives of all the three national communities in Bosnia. Or let me put it another way, representatives of the ruling political parties, the SDA, the HDZ, and the SDS. So the SDS leaders have now gotten themselves into negotiations in an international forum. The first session of those negotiations was held in Sarajevo on the 13th of February, that is, the day before this meeting. The reference to the map could be a reference to a map that was produced at that meeting. I do not know what map it is or whose map -- who may have produced it, but I think that may be the reference. The reference to 61 per cent of the territory is not entirely clear either. Since he refers to Mr. Izetbegovic, and because, as we know, there were negotiations going on between the Bosnian Serbs and the Bosnian Croats, that percentage could represent the total of territory which was being assigned in that map to the Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Croats. Or it could be the territory that the Bosnian Serb leaders were claiming for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, Mr. Treanor. I neglected to ask you, although you may have mentioned it, for the B/C/S reference to that page, if you have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The ERN number is 04002198, and this passage begins at the very bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, counsel previously noted that Mr. Krajisnik did not have in front of him the B/C/S versions of the intercepts because, under normal circumstances, he was following them on screen and listening to the contents. This document, however, is found in the intercepts binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the situation. Our case manager and I have actually the intercepts binder, because normally, of course, the intercepts are played and we can hear them, and of course, importantly, Mr. Krajisnik can hear them. But in the intercepts binder is, of course, this particular speech, so Mr. Krajisnik doesn't have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So whenever it comes to transcripts not of any intercepted telephone conversations, we have a problem. What I -- do we have a -- at the end of the English version, we find B/C/S versions. So, for example, in 27, the English version is -- takes 31 pages, and then at least, even in my English, or my binder, I find the B/C/S text. Does Mr. Krajisnik -- could someone perhaps give, if it were only temporarily, a copy to Mr. Krajisnik of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's what we're actually proposing to do, because we actually received two copies of most of these folders from the Prosecution, that is, a folder with just English and a folder with English and B/C/S. But in relation to the intercepts folder all we received was one folder with both English and B/C/S. But for the purposes of what we're dealing with now, we'll hand over to Mr. Krajisnik the B/C/S copy of this particular speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I think you would have 20 minutes for that, because we're about to have a break, Mr. Tieger, unless there would be -- this would not be a suitable moment. But then it would have to be within one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It appears to be a suitable moment, for more than one reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Preliminarily, with reference to the precise pagination and format of the speech, there is a technical explanation for that. I'm not sure the Court -- how deeply the Court wants me to get into that, but it's fairly clear. When a Word document is converted into the electronic format, apparently that results in a slight deviation, which is normally not significant. But because we have the enumerated figures at the side of the page, for this particular document, it was noticeable and played a role in identifying the particular location of any segment. We're having it reprinted in the -- from the TIF format in this particular case because of the unique circumstances of the speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation, Mr. Tieger. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, before the break you mentioned the negotiations which had begun shortly before the Deputies' Club meeting at which Dr. Karadzic's speech was given. Do his remarks in that speech reflect the steps that should be taken in conjunction with those ongoing negotiations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've seen the reference to the map here. I'm not sure of any other direct -- possibly direct connection at this time with the negotiations. Maybe we'll see that in the further excerpts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to the next highlighted portion of the speech, which is found on pages 5 and 6 of the English translation, and if you could identify the B/C/S page numbers on which those appear.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This excerpt appears on page 04002200, and it's in the middle of that page in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the highlighted portion that appears in English is found at the bottom -- or begins at the bottom quarter of page 5 with the statement: "The factual situation is so-and-so, now it is so, now it's up to us." And continues to the bottom of the page and then on, on to the next page, which we'll identify when it appears on screen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, in this portion of his remarks, Dr. Karadzic makes reference to the second degree, or, as it seems to be translated here, stage number 2, which seems to be a reference to the 19 December 1991 instructions, that is, the Variant A and B document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that reference, Mr. Treanor, found at the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the very bottom of the page in the translation, which goes on to the next page. In the original, it's all on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, that highlighted section begins at the top of the page, of course, and continues to the sentence: "They Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. will not strive to establish cantonal authorities, that is, some authorities of their republic, so you have a big advantage over them now." And again, the reference is found at the top of that page, that is, "Therefore, the stage number two, the second stage in smaller or bigger variations, but you have to implement that slowly now."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, any further comments in that particular highlighted section?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 11 of the English translation, you've highlighted a section that begins: "Krajisnik and I went to Titograd twice," and continues on to the bottom of the page and, obviously, on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in relation to that, if we could have the B/C/S identifying page number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I just found that location. It is 04002204, and it's toward the bottom of that page. Here Dr. Karadzic addresses the subject of relations between Serbia and Montenegro and the relations of the Bosnian Serbs with those two republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, the highlighted section continues on to page 12 of the English translation, concluding that sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to page 14 of the English translation. You have highlighted a section that appears in approximately the bottom third of the page and begins: "The map that we saw includes over 90 per cent of Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This excerpt begins on page 04002206, at the bottom, and continues on to the next page. In it, Dr. Karadzic refers to the good outlook which seems to exist within the framework of the negotiations. Again, the reference to the map. The good outlook that seems to be offered for keeping as many Serbs as possible within one entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And he seems to be saying that it won't be everybody, but it's something that we can be satisfied with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as indicated before, that highlighted section continues on to page 15, with the completion of the sentence begun on the previous page, thereby ending with the line: "Then to have all this thousand, a million and a half Serbs, to stay in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The idea voiced here just above that seems to be similar to the idea that we saw in the meeting with the Croatian officials at the beginning of January, that is, once these -- the boundaries of the ethnic communities, the new entities and the transformed BH were established, that there would probably be a process of people migrating to their own entity if they didn't live in it already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to addressing the negotiations that are ongoing, the call for stage 2 to begin in addition, does Dr. Karadzic express a view of why ethnic separation is necessary?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a section which I have selected which I hope we're going to see now, in which he addresses his views on the ability of Muslims to live with others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to the highlighted section which begins at the bottom of page 18, last two sentences of that page, beginning: "Gentlemen, the moment the Muslims get hold of the fundamentalism, they cannot live anywhere, with nobody --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honours. I don't have the page number again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I saw you struggling with it, but since I was informed that I should not start speaking until the translation is finished, I tried to obey that. But, Mr. Treanor, would you please indicate where to find --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was waiting for an appropriate moment to jump in as well, Your Honour. This is at the very top of 04002210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, as long as we are in this document, the 0400 is always there, so if you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- give the last four digits, that would be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have here now the reprinted versions of the speech. I don't know if the Court finds it necessary to distribute them at this moment or if we should wait for an appropriate break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we could do that during the break and continue now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Treanor, you were about to address the selected portions beginning at the bottom of 18 and continuing on to 19.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this section, as I think I said, Dr. Karadzic addresses his views -- expresses his views on the ability of Muslims to live with other peoples in the same state, and he goes on to quote the poet Njegos, who we've already referred to, the great Montenegrin national poet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that found in the section where Mr. Karadzic mentions two soups would not get mixed in the same pot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The top of the page, Dr. Karadzic refers to India and Kashmir, India and Pakistan in dramatic exchanges of population.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a theme that we'll see rising again in the course of later remarks by Dr. Karadzic in other speeches?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of his favourite analogies, similar to the one about the plebiscite in Carinthia, which he continually refers to. He likes to use this analogy of India and Pakistan in describing the prospects for the possibilities of life between Muslims and non-Muslims in the same state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, I had indicated previously that the selected portion or the highlighted portion which began at the bottom of page 18 continues on to 19. It is found at the beginning of the page, of course, where it says: "Nowhere." And continues with: "India and Kashmir." And ends with the two lines: "We are really something different, something different, and we should not hide that. We are not brothers. We must know that."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And turning to page 24 of the English translation, does Dr. Karadzic call again for the introduction of the second level?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in terms of ensuring that the page references go a little more cleanly, I was wondering if Mr. Tieger, when he mentions the English page, could then immediately mention the B/C/S page, or call upon the witness to go to the B/C/S page, so that Mr. Krajisnik can find the page before Mr. Tieger starts formulating the rest of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that could be a very practical way of proceeding. Whenever you make reference to a page, you'd stop immediately, Mr. Tieger, and then Mr. Treanor would indicate what page in the B/C/S that would be. Yes. Please proceed. We are now on page 24 of the English translation, and that would be, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the top of 2214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the highlighted section, Your Honour, begins with the words: "They must be 100 per cent sure, to where a certain move leads." And it ends then with the calling of a break. "I am asking you for a break. What do you say, half an hour?" The reference in the translation, as I can see, to the second level, is the same expression that we saw before and is in the Variant A and B documents, which would literally be translated as the second degree, or could be literally translated as the second degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is a reference, Mr. Treanor, to the portion of the highlighted section where Dr. Karadzic says: "That is why we called you today, to intensify, to introduce the second level, and to intensify the functioning of the government at any cost and on every single millimetre of our territory."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, the last highlighted section is found on page 26 of the English translation. I know Mr. Treanor will address the B/C/S portion, but I note that we will be playing that on the Sanction on -- through the tape. So that will be the equivalent of an intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if you just have that page number handy for reference.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unless I'm mistaken, it would be on 2215.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, it's noted --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the middle of that page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That will be available to Mr. Krajisnik orally, or audibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, any comment on that last highlighted section of the speech?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Just to remind the Court, here we see a reference to the Belgrade Initiative, which we considered earlier, and Dr. Karadzic saying that at this point in time, that even that would not be enough for the Bosnian Serb leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we can turn now to tab 88. That is the 7th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was held on 15 February 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the main business of this session was to consider the drafts that had been prepared of a constitution and related legislation necessary to set up government organs within the proclaimed Serbian Republic. If the Court will recall, at the session on the 25th of January, there had been some discussion of that, and the necessity for pushing that forward, a deadline of the 15th of February had been mentioned. In fact, in the published version of the decisions of that session, that deadline is not mentioned. It refers to doing it as soon as possible, but in fact we see them meeting here on the 15th of February to consider precisely that package of legislation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one question in respect of this document which we find under tab 88. The English version says, "Tape-recording," whereas the B/C/S version starts with the word which very much looks like, "Stenographic." Is that the same, or could you explain whether there's any difference. Because stenographic recording of a meeting is perhaps not the same as tape-recording.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There are, in fact, two records of this meeting, both the stenographic record and a transcript of the tape-recording. The copy I am looking at, the document I am looking at, is the transcript of the audio recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is that exactly the same as the B/C/S version which starts with the stenographic recording? Because Mr. Krajisnik, I take it, will look at the B/C/S version of this document. So I just wonder whether it's exactly the same or whether there are any differences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the transcript of the recording and the stenographic record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I see, at least, that the front page, that, to the extent I can understand it, that the one is referring to another technique than the other one, and I just wondered whether this had any consequences in the text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two documents are not exactly the same. The transcript of the tape-recording is 67 pages long and the stenographic record is 61 pages long. The stenographic record tends to be cleaned up a little bit to -- from the format point of view, to make the -- various decisions that were adopted stand out better in the text, that type of thing. At certain points, it summarises, say, the adoption of a decision, rather than giving verbatim what is said, and it does vary from session to session, where we do have two records, sometimes we see the stenographic record summarising rather than reporting verbatim discussion, and there are occasional differences in the wording between the speeches that are reproduced in both of them. So the two documents are not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please keep that in mind when we discuss these documents, that there could be some confusion as far as details are concerned. But I also do understand that mainly it is representing the same spoken words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the main, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is a bit concerned about different versions and would like to ensure that whatever English versions we work Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. off is a precise translation of the document Mr. Krajisnik has in front of him. So therefore, since I have got in my -- in binder 8 both versions, English and B/C/S, if we cannot be sure that the document with -- starting with the ERN number 00898063 would be exactly the same document as the English document 01105038, if that is not for certain, then I would invite the Prosecution to move forwards and, as soon as they have provided Mr. Krajisnik with exactly the same document, that you can come back to this issue, but not deal with it on the basis of two documents that are not exactly the same. Do I understand that these documents are not exactly the same, the B/C/S version indicating that it's a stenographic report, and the English one saying that it's a tape-recording? Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not have the B/C/S version in front of me, but I come to the same conclusion the Court did, based on the information just provided, and that is that the stenographic B/C/S version was inadvertently conjoined with the English translation of the tape, and I agree; we will attempt, and I trust will have forthwith, the corresponding B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's, then, proceed in this way, and as soon as the matter has been settled, that you could come back to this issue, but not at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, I'd like to move forward to tab 90 of the binder. That contains an English translation of a letter of 20 February 1992 from the SDS Executive Board to SDS municipal boards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about that particular document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the Court can see, this is a letter from the secretary of the Executive Board of the SDS to the municipal boards, sending to them a copy of a proclamation to the Serbian people in BH in connection with the upcoming referendum and asking them to assure that that proclamation is distributed to every Serbian home. As we've seen before on a number of occasions, the SDS was very anxious, Dr. Karadzic in particular, that the members of the local community boards be responsible for a certain number of Serbian homes, so that they were in a position to get information and distribute materials to every Serbian home in the republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 of that document, or to an attachment to that document. You've highlighted the second paragraph, which begins: "By voting on the referendum of citizens."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here we see in this particular document which was to be distributed the fear expressed of the establishment of an Islamic state in BH, should the Serbs become a national minority in somebody else's state, in this case it was referred to as an Islamic state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that tab 91 contains a proclamation to the Serbian people. BH is -- are there significant differences between the document we've just reviewed and that document that require us to call it on screen and --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The content of that document is quite a bit different. The thrust of that -- this proclamation is that the Serbian people have already had their plebiscite, so there's no necessity for them to vote in the upcoming referendum. But on the other hand, nothing should be done to disturb the carrying out of that referendum, since the other two peoples are entitled to have their vote as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn next, then, to tab 92, the next document you've selected. This is a document headed, "Presidency of social federative Republic of Yugoslavia." Dated 24 February 1992, indicating, "Deliver immediately."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an invitation to a meeting in Belgrade of the Presidency of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. I'm looking at the date. There are two similar documents. There had been an invitation to -- issued on the 21st of February to a session on the 27th of February, and on the 24th of February, the invitees were informed that the date of the meeting had been postponed to the 28th. The people invited are basically the -- aside from the leaders of the -- of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Montenegro, the leaders of the Bosnian Serbs and the Croatian Serbs, including Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, Dr. Koljevic, and Dr. Plavsic. Here we see the first letter that went out on the 21st of September, and that letter specifies what the agenda for the meeting will be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the portion presently highlighted on the screen?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And under number 3, the Court will see that one of the items is: "Consideration of the basis of the constitutional order and functioning of Yugoslavia as a joint state."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on February 25th, 1992, the 8th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina was held. And that's found at tab 93 and I believe is the next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before we get into this document, I would like to point out to the Court that the negotiations under international auspices among the three parties in BH were continuing. There was a session in Lisbon on the 21st and 22nd of February, possibly continuing into the 23rd, at which an agreement was reached, in principle, on a statement of principles for the new constitutional arrangement for BH. And there was much discussion of those negotiations at the session of the 25th with Dr. Karadzic and the others who participated in those discussions, including, I believe, Dr. Koljevic and Mr. Krajisnik, informed the deputies of what went on there. The statement of principles included a number of points, including the internal organisation of BH. One of the important points, though, especially in connection with the maps we've seen mentioned, was the -- at the end of the document, the definition of the constituent units. Just to cite a bit from that document adopted in Lisbon on the 23rd, it states that: "The territory of the constituent units would be defined on the basis of the 1971, 1989, or 1991 census, and the existing communes, with only such small adjustments as may be clearly justified. In such a way, the communes," that means the municipalities, "where one particular nation is clearly in a majority are grouped together into the appropriate constituent unit. A state may have several separate of parts," and it goes on about arbitration commission and that type of thing. So the idea there agreed in principle was that there would be constituent units composed basically of groups of the existing municipalities in BH and that the constituent units themselves could possibly be in more than one part, that is, not entirely continuous territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first highlighted portion of the session of 25 February appears on page 9 of the English translation, and that would be what page of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am looking at the stenographic record, and that would be Dr. Karadzic speaking at the bottom of SA 025444.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I believe this previous problem was caused -- the previous need to refer to ERN numbers was a reflection of a particular document which I think bore some odd pagination. I have the B/C/S numbers for this particular document and can refer directly to the corresponding B/C/S page. That would be the bottom of page 9 and top of page 10 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you are able to mention the B/C/S page numbers, then of course it would solve the problem as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first highlighted section is found in the middle of the page. It is the third full paragraph, beginning: "Members of minorities in a constituent unit."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is part of - and I think we're going to see a bit more - of Dr. Karadzic's report to the deputies on the results of the discussions in Lisbon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reference from: "Major relocations from one unit to another without a special permit are not foreseen, as that would upset the national mix," is that a reference to a concern that was expressed to negotiators and that the Bosnian Serb leaders attempted to build into the --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
